text:
acme-cs: Heads up — ACME reported a regression after today's rollout of speculative decoding (we shipped the draft rollout at ~10:12 UTC). They say answers are shorter, more hallucinations, and a couple of important fields are missing in structured outputs. Customer is escalated and blocked on a demo. Request IDs & sample pairs below.

marta.support: Thanks for flagging. Can you paste request IDs + a representative prompt/expected vs actual output? Also what route/model they hit (we need model id & variant).

acme-cs: Sending the two repros the customer attached. They are hitting route `acme-qna` which routes to `rwd-13b` and we had speculative-decoding enabled as part of the draft rollout.

acme-cs: Prompt 1:
"""
Customer prompt: 
"Summarize the following meeting notes and list action items with owners."
Notes: "Discussed API quotas. Sam -> follow up on quota increase. We also need to schedule security review. Jenna to prepare docs."
"""

Expected (previously):
"- Sam: follow up on quota increase (due 4/20)
- Jenna: prepare security review docs (due 4/22)
Concise 4-line summary: ...)"

Actual (after rollout):
"Follow up on quotas and security review. Assign owners."  <-- missing owners and dates, vague.

acme-cs: Request IDs: `req_2026_04_05_74a3`, `req_2026_04_05_74a4`. Timestamps ~ 2026-04-05T10:17:03Z and 10:18:11Z.

ben.ml: Thanks — this smells like the speculative/draft path changed decoding heuristics. Two quick Qs:
1) Was the rollout using an alternate logits processor or early-stopping config?
2) Did we change the `max_output_tokens` or `stop` token handling for the draft variant?

riley.sre: Also confirm rollout percentage and whether traffic was routed via smart-routing. If only canary traffic saw it we can rollback the feature flag for the draft path.

deploy-bot: deploy: spec-decoding-draft v1.4 started rollout at 2026-04-05T10:12:08Z -> rollout 30% to `rwd-13b` on region us-west-2. CID: deploy-84b2

marta.support: Repro steps from our side (quick):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{\n  "model": "rwd-13b",\n  "route": "acme-qna",\n  "prompt": "Summarize the following meeting notes and list action items with owners.\nNotes: \"Discussed API quotas. Sam -> follow up on quota increase. We also need to schedule security review. Jenna to prepare docs.\"",\n  "max_output_tokens": 200,\n  "speculative_decoding": true\n}'

Replace `speculative_decoding` with `false` to test pinned behavior.

elena.cs: I ran the above and attached the exact outputs in our customer transcript. Short snippet: the spec-decoding path returned: "Follow up on quotas and security review. Assign owners." while non-spec path returned the correct action items with owners.

ben.ml: Can you also pull the token-level logits / length distribution for those request IDs? If speculative decoding dropped tokens early due to a bad early stopping heuristic, we'll see a sharp spike in probability mass on EOS token at a specific step.

marta.support: Pasted server logs for req_2026_04_05_74a3:
```
[10:17:03.121] req_2026_04_05_74a3 route=acme-qna variant=spec-draft model=rwd-13b user=acme token_usage=112 latency=420ms decode_path=speculative seed=1821 early_stop_triggered=true eos_prob=0.87
[10:17:03.123] generation truncated at step 18, emitted eos
```

marta.support: For the non-spec path (same prompt):
```
[10:20:11.662] req_2026_04_05_74b1 route=acme-qna variant=stable model=rwd-13b token_usage=198 latency=880ms decode_path=standard seed=1821 early_stop_triggered=false eos_prob=0.02
```

ben.ml: That early_stop_triggered + eos_prob=0.87 is the smoking gun. Speculative decoding likely ran a shallow scorer that prematurely favored EOS in some contexts. Where we got bitten last time: mismatch between draft and stable top-k/p_top or temperature schedule.

riley.sre: Agreed — mitigation plan: 1) roll the feature flag for `spec-decoding-draft` to 0% for `acme-qna` 2) route affected customer traffic to `stable` variant 3) pin customer route to stable until QA signoff. I can execute rollback if someone gives the green light.

marta.support: Customer-facing mitigation message (draft): "We've identified a decoding optimization introduced in a recent rollout that can shorten answers in some prompts. We are rolling back the optimization for your route and will follow up with validation steps. Sorry for the disruption." Thoughts?

ben.ml: Approve message. We'll also add a short-term fix on server side: force disable early_stop for spec path until we tune the eos heuristics. I'll run a small eval suite across ~200 of ACME's prompts to measure deltas.

elena.cs: Please include reference to request IDs and the ETA for rollback. The customer asked for ETA within 30 minutes.

riley.sre: I'll roll back now. Command I'm using (internal admin CLI):
```
rbctl set-rollout --route acme-qna --feature spec-decoding-draft --percent 0 --reason "regression on rwd-13b; acme escalated"
rbctl pin-route --route acme-qna --variant stable
```

deploy-bot: action: rollout-update deploy-84b2 -> spec-decoding-draft set to 0% for route acme-qna by riley.sre at 2026-04-05T10:32:48Z

marta.support: Confirmed pinned to `stable` variant for `acme-qna`. Customer notified — they acknowledged and will re-run their demo.

ben.ml: I'll run the eval and send a diff report. Early hypothesis: tuning the speculative scorer (reduce eos bias, align top-k) and adding an EOS-suppression window for first N tokens should materially improve recall/length.

marta.support: After action items:
- riley.sre: rollback + pin (done)
- ben.ml: run eval + PR with tuned eos schedule
- eng-oncall: add a regression alert on per-route structured-output F1 for next rollout
- marta.support: follow up with customer and confirm closure

elena.cs: Customer said the pinned route fixed the immediate problem — demo succeeded. They'll keep an eye out and report anything else.

ben.ml: I'll open a short incident postmortem and add a checklist for speculative/draft rollouts (eval on structured-output prompts, eos-prob sanity checks, per-route canary throttles).

marta.support: Nice work team. We'll keep this thread updated with the postmortem link and the tuned rollout plan. :thumbsup:

riley.sre: Adding to runbook: if speculative path shows early_stop_triggered=true with eos_prob > 0.5 on < 25 tokens and customer reports loss of content -> immediate rollback.

deploy-bot: incident-note: rollback completed; ticket INC-2026-042 marked acknowledged.

marta.support: Closing notes: customer happy for now; scheduling postmortem with eng-ml next week to validate new scoring changes before re-rollout.
